tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Artists and Art Movements

questions.question: Create a series of experimental studies exploring artists and art movements. Annotate your process.
questions.correctAnswer: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to artists and art movements, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes.

questions.question: Research an artist or designer who works with artists and art movements. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work.
questions.correctAnswer: A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with artists and art movements. Which approaches were most successful and why?
questions.correctAnswer: A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on Artists and Art Movements

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Research two artists from different movements. Write a critical analysis comparing their approaches, explaining their contexts, and showing how each has influenced the development of your personal project. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: name specific artworks with dates; analyse HOW and WHY artists work, not just describe; use specialist vocabulary; understand the social/cultural/political context; make CLEAR connections between researched artists and own work. Mark scheme: AO1 (develop through investigation) + AO2 (refine through experimentation) + AO3 (record ideas and observations) + AO4 (present personal response) = total marks
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
